A1.justification: Both complete 19-page PDFs describe the same GraphAny work and include Appendices A-E. Text and visual inspection support reliable comparison; pages 4-19 have identical text and rendered content.

before.justification: v3 reports original node-classification experiments across 31 datasets, runtime measurements, attention analyses, and ablations in Section 4 and Appendices D-E.

after.justification: v5 retains the original classification results, runtime measurements, attention analyses, and main-text and appendix ablations.

M1.justification: Both versions use analytical LinearGNN predictions fused by attention based on entropy-normalized distances. Section 3, the training procedure in Appendix C, and the operator variants in Appendix E are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same 31 node-classification datasets, with separate GraphAny models trained on Cora, Wisconsin, Arxiv, and Products. The 27 common held-out datasets and the supplementary ACM-GNN evaluation subset are unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain MLP, GCN, GAT, label propagation, and the five LinearGNN baselines. Appendix E retains MeanAgg in the operator ablation and ACM-SGC and ACM-GCN in Table 6.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1 and Appendices B-C retain identical splits, accuracy metrics, training budgets, model configurations, and hyperparameter searches. The supplementary evaluation procedures in Appendix E are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The feature-distribution and attention analyses remain unchanged, as do the entropy-normalization and attention-parameterization ablations in Figures 8-9. Appendix E.1 retains the same LinearGNN, Chebyshev, and personalized PageRank operator ablations.

E5.justification: Appendix C specifies the same five random seeds, {0, 1, 2, 3, 4}, in both versions. The uncertainty values and graphical uncertainty displays are identical, with no change in reporting practices.

E6.justification: All numerical results and plotted findings are retained. Examples include GraphAny (Wisconsin)'s 67.26 ± 0.20% total average across 31 graphs in Table 2 and GraphAny's 6.37-minute runtime in Table 1; Appendix D-E results are also identical.

T1.justification: The analytical solution, invariance definitions and derivations, complexity analysis, and Appendix A permutation-invariance proofs are unchanged. Appendix E's mathematical descriptions of alternative graph operators are also retained.

C1.justification: The claims about fully-inductive inference, arbitrary feature and label spaces, novelty, accuracy, and speed remain unchanged. Replacing 'the fully-inductive setup' with 'a fully-inductive setup' in the abstract does not substantively change these claims.

C2.justification: Both retain the same explanations of entropy normalization, attention behavior, and transfer from small training graphs. Appendix E's interpretations of operator behavior and qualifications concerning the ACM-GNN comparison are unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains identical implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, memory requirements, and baseline tuning instructions. The reported code-release link and other hyperlink targets are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography contain the same cited works and positioning relative to inductive GNNs, labels-as-features methods, and graph foundation models. No prior-work relationship or novelty claim changes.

P1.justification: v5 makes tiny editorial changes: 'the' becomes 'a' in the abstract, author superscript punctuation is corrected, and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. The prose, section order, and narrative otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn and enlarged, changing its illustrative graphs and matrix arrangement while preserving its meaning and caption. Spacing changes on pages 2-3 move one unchanged contribution bullet to page 3; all other figures and tables are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v5 refreshes Figure 2 and makes small wording and layout edits, while retaining the scientific content and all appendices unchanged. These cosmetic revisions do not materially change clarity, evidential support, or reproducibility, so overall paper quality remains effectively the same.
